reason: The tenant reports a hot, burning smell and a warm socket (event-001). At 16:42 she says the smell persists and nobody has inspected (event-025). Warmth near the socket was still noticed at event-017. A 10-year-old child is in the home (event-004). I treat this as a reported electrical fire risk, so it is P0 until verified. The landlord only offered a handyman who cannot do fixed wiring, has no test equipment and did not enter (events 6, 11, 15, 23). The landlord has given no electrician approval and has not answered the access question or the latest request (events 16, 20, 24). So waiting or chasing alone would leave the risk uncontrolled. The agency cannot approve spend, so a person on call must decide on an emergency electrician. No emergency guidance had been given (event-009, event-025). I staged immediate safety advice to the tenant: keep appliances off, leave and call 999 if there is smoke, sparks or a stronger smell, and isolate the circuit only if she can identify it with certainty. No documents conflict. Unknowns are the real condition of the socket and the landlord's decision.

actions.body: Hi Nora, thank you for the update. Please keep the kettle and all other appliances away from that socket and do not touch its face. If you see smoke, sparks or scorch marks, hear crackling or buzzing, or the smell gets stronger, leave the flat with your son straight away and call 999. Please do not open or work on the socket yourself. If you can identify the kitchen breaker with certainty you may switch it off, but do not guess or take any risk. We have passed this to our on-call team as urgent and will update you as soon as a person has reviewed it. Northbridge Lettings (Maya Chen)
actions.note: Recorded in the local outbox (no external delivery connected).
